notes: 9 of 27 assertions flip from fail to pass with the skill, 17 pass in both arms, 1 flips the other way (eval 1: 'no untaught fact'), none fail in both. Every eval improved: eval 0 7/9 to 9/9, eval 1 5/9 to 8/9, eval 2 7/9 to 9/9.

All 6 opener/closer assertions pass in both arms. The baseline Sonnet run already runs under this user's CLAUDE.md (terse mode, no closers), so 'no Great question / Let me know' does not measure skill value in this environment.

The clearest wins are the action-shape rules. 'First line is an action' flipped in both evals that test it (0 and 1); the baselines opened with a context sentence ('GitHub Actions reads YAML files from...', 'Node 24 isn't a documented cause...'). 'Ends with one next action' and 'time estimate in concrete units' flipped in eval 1; the baseline ended on a caveat paragraph and gave no estimate.
'Define the term in the same sentence it first appears' flipped in evals 0 and 1. The baselines defined EADDRINUSE two sentences later and never defined 'workflow' or 'job' at all.

Eval 2 (explain): the baseline answered the logout premise with a flat 'yes, it's true' and only qualified it several sentences later; the skill run framed the condition up front. The baseline also wrote 4.7 KB with zero headers, which the skill's explain override asks for.

Regression (eval 1, with skill): the reply says the .github/workflows folders 'don't exist yet, so create those too' but gives no command for it; the baseline gave 'mkdir -p .github/workflows'. Plausible mechanism: 'lead with the action, fewest steps' compressed out a step the reader still needs. One observation.

Assertion 'numbered list, max 5 items' passed the baseline on bold numbered section headings (longest same-level run = 1), so it is lenient as written and non-discriminating. For iteration 2, reword to 'a numbered list where each item is one bounded action'.

Assertion 'headers or another skimmable structure' is graded header-only by the script; the eval 2 baseline had two 4-item lists and no headers. Either reword to 'uses headers' (matching the skill's explain override) or make the script count lists. Decide before iteration 2.

Cost: +145 s mean time and +26.5k tokens (+23%) with the skill, at n=1 per eval and high variance (baseline times ranged 183 s to 513 s). Each with-skill run spent one extra tool turn reading the 11.7 KB SKILL.md, and subagent token totals accumulate per turn, so one extra turn plausibly explains most of the delta. Not verified.

Sample size is 1 run per eval per arm across 3 evals. The +0.26 delta is directionally clear because every eval improved, but each per-assertion flip is a single observation; rerun with 2 to 3 runs per arm before treating any single assertion as settled.
